strategy.audience: Non-technical small-business leader, AI level 0-6 of 10 (POSITIONING.md §4): an owner, operations lead or team lead in a 5-50 person company who is responsible for one repeated process and has tried ChatGPT but has no repeatable way of using it at work. Specifically anyone about to trial a tool for a process that already lives in an inbox, a spreadsheet or a calendar.
strategy.concept: A tool is only as useful as the systems it can already reach, and on Thursday our own weekly run proved it twice: one source went silent, and one destination that had answered three days earlier stopped answering because it had been moved at the other end.

filter.ai_boundary: The tool moves and drafts between named systems. The human owns the account access, decides what the tool may see, and stays responsible for whether a connection is actually open rather than merely listed.
filter.friction: A tool that cannot read and write those three systems turns the work into copying and pasting, which is more manual work than there was before. And 'supported' on a feature page is not the same as connected: a connection can be live on Monday, be removed at the other end, and be gone by Thursday without anything on the feature page changing.
filter.next_action: Write down the three systems your process actually touches and check them, by name, against the tool's own integrations page before the trial starts.
filter.process: Any repeated task whose inputs and outputs already sit in an inbox, a spreadsheet and a calendar - taking an enquiry, recording it, and putting a slot in the diary for it.

strategy.objective: Get the viewer to open the integrations page before the feature page, check three named systems against it before a trial starts, and check again that each one is still answering.
strategy.promise: A two-minute check, before you trial anything, that tells you whether the tool can touch the work you actually do.
strategy.rationale: Naming specific things is the only lexical feature that predicts reach and survives creator normalisation (distinct entities vs view_lift +0.161 pooled, +0.198 within creators), and this reel is built entirely out of names. The references supply grammar: each destination introduced at the moment the workflow needs it (DNA7-d3o5sQ), two identically shaped steps each closing on a concrete count (DZU9x_1AY2t), a connector being attached on screen in real time (Db9MT-axxcO), and the everybody-wants-X-but-nobody-does-Y opening with the friction named as a concrete act (DVZGBgTk6zz).

title: Supported is not the same as connected

traceability.evidence_summary: Our own weekly run is a chain of six named systems and on 2026-09-10 two of the links failed for two different reasons. The free public-profile source returned nothing five times in a row and 0 of 130 profiles were updated. Three separate steps failed with the same 404 from the notes tool - two on one database, one on another - while the one step in the same run that wrote to a page rather than a database succeeded. The same destination had answered three days earlier, on 2026-09-07, when steps 7 and 10 both went through: the connection existed and was removed at the other end. The four references contribute grammar only: destinations named in dependency order over a 56-second unbroken screen take (DNA7-d3o5sQ, ungated, 23.3 shares/1k), two identically shaped steps each closing on a count (DZU9x_1AY2t, 25.8 shares/1k), a connection shown being made on the settings screen (Db9MT-axxcO, best combined 47.9 and 68.9 per 1k on only 1.62x lift) and a friction-then-promise opening (DVZGBgTk6zz, 34.8 shares/1k).
traceability.original_synthesis: The corpus names tools constantly and integrations almost never; the connector list is treated as plumbing rather than as the buying decision. The failure is ours, dated and quotable from two run logs three days apart, and it is the more interesting failure mode because the connection was live on Monday and gone by Thursday with nothing on the tool's side changing. The reel names no vendor, makes no time or cost claim, and hands over a check rather than a tool recommendation.
traceability.why_better_than_generic: A generic AI script would list five tools that integrate with Gmail. This one shows a single item crossing three ordinary systems, then produces two real logs three days apart in which the same supported connection worked and then did not, for a reason that has nothing to do with the model - and it separates supported, connected and still connected, which is the sentence the viewer can use in a sales call. Naming specific things is the only lexical feature that predicts reach and survives creator normalisation (+0.161 pooled, +0.198 within creators), and every load-bearing noun in this script is a name.
